title: NICE NG12 — breast lump referral
text: NICE recommends a suspected cancer pathway referral for women aged 30 and over with an unexplained breast lump, with or without pain. Under 30, an unexplained breast lump should be considered for non-urgent referral.

title: NICE NG12 — nipple changes
text: For women aged 50 and over, discharge, retraction or other changes of concern in one nipple only should lead to a suspected cancer pathway referral.

title: NICE NG12 — breast skin changes and armpit lumps
text: Skin changes that suggest breast cancer, such as dimpling or puckering, and an unexplained lump in the armpit in women aged 30 and over should be considered for a suspected cancer pathway referral.

title: NICE NG12 — ovarian cancer symptoms
text: If a woman, especially one aged 50 or over, reports persistent or frequent bloating, feeling full quickly or loss of appetite, pelvic or abdominal pain, or needing to pass urine urgently or often, primary care should arrange tests starting with a CA125 blood test, followed by an ultrasound if it is raised.

title: NICE NG12 — pelvic mass or ascites
text: An urgent referral is recommended if examination finds fluid in the abdomen (ascites) or a pelvic or abdominal mass that is not obviously caused by fibroids.

title: NICE NG12 — post-menopausal bleeding
text: Vaginal bleeding more than 12 months after periods have stopped is post-menopausal bleeding. Women aged 55 and over with post-menopausal bleeding should have a suspected cancer pathway referral, and it should be considered for younger women too.

title: NICE CKS — cervical symptoms needing examination
text: Bleeding after sex, bleeding between periods, and persistent unusual vaginal discharge are symptoms that should be assessed by a clinician, including examination of the cervix. A normal past screening result does not rule out a problem if symptoms are present.

title: WHO — cervical cancer screening
text: Cervical cancer is one of the most preventable cancers. WHO recommends regular screening with HPV testing from age 30, and early detection allows effective treatment. Symptoms should not wait for the next routine screening.

title: WHO — breast cancer early diagnosis
text: Most breast lumps are not cancer, but early assessment of a new lump or change greatly improves outcomes. Delays often come from fear or stigma, and prompt evaluation is the most important step.
